title: These Dolphins Wear Sponges on Their Faces to Hunt
subject: bottlenose dolphin

scenes.text: Some dolphins hunt wearing a sponge on their face.
In Shark Bay, Western Australia, bottlenose dolphins tear a sponge off the seabed and carry it on their beak.
They're hunting fish buried in rough sand. The sponge works like a glove for the snout.
Those fish have no swim bladder, so the dolphin's sonar can't find them. It has to dig.
Nobody invents this alone. Calves spend years with their mothers, learning it by watching.
In one study, 91 percent of daughters picked it up, against 25 percent of sons.

description:
Some dolphins hunt wearing a sponge on their face.
In Shark Bay, bottlenose dolphins use sponges as snout protection, a skill passed mainly from mothers to daughters.
What's the smartest animal trick you've seen?
